thread:
amanda: quick follow-up to the sealed-bundle RFC — proposal to avoid wall-clock reliance for signature rotation in air-gapped installs. thinking out loud.
raj: +1 on not depending on NTP. a lot of remote customers can't guarantee time. what's the alternative?
josh: sequence-based rotation? include a monotonic lease/sequence number inside the bundle that the agent enforces.
amanda: exactly. instead of time TTL on signing keys, we ship a "lease_seq" that increments with every approved bundle. agent keeps latest_applied_seq in durable storage and rejects bundles with seq <= latest_applied_seq unless operator performs an explicit force-update.
liz: how do we prevent a replay where an attacker drops a new bundle and resends an old one to revert? if agent only stores seq, someone could replay an older bundle with higher seq if they tampered with seq values.
raj: that's why we tie seq to a hash-chain anchored by signatures. each bundle includes: content_hash, lease_seq, prev_bundle_hash, and a rotation_proof (sig by previous key). agent verifies chain integrity before applying. replay of arbitrary older content would fail because prev_bundle_hash won't match stored last_applied_hash.
amanda: here's a minimal example manifest snippet we discussed:
```yaml
bundle:
  content_hash: "sha256:3f5e..."
lease_seq: 42
rotation:
  prev_key_fingerprint: "ab12:..."
  new_key_fingerprint: "cd34:..."
  rotation_proof_sig: "BASE64_SIG=="
prev_bundle_hash: "sha256:deadbeef..."
```
josh: that looks good. rotation_proof_sig is the previous key signing (new_key_fingerprint + content_hash + lease_seq)?
amanda: yes, the idea is previous key signs a tuple (new_key_fingerprint, content_hash, lease_seq, prev_bundle_hash). that gives us a verifiable rotation step without needing time.
liz: operational question: what if the device was factory-reset and loses last_applied_hash? we need a safe recovery flow that doesn't allow silent downgrade. maybe require an operator-provided short-lived "recovery token" signed by a root offline KMS, plus an audit log entry.
raj: agreed. recovery should be explicit and auditable. we can require a double-signed recovery artifact: operator-signature + internal-ops countersign if customer opted in. fallback path must be documented and gated.
amanda: note on key management: for Private deployments we can integrate HSM/KMS for local key storage. For pure air-gapped installs, we rely on the sealed-bundle rotation chain; the initial root key is provisioned manually during install.
josh: tradeoff: storing last_applied_hash as a durable monotonic store increases complexity for lightweight agents. do we expect every on-prem node to have persistent encrypted storage?
liz: yes, minimal requirement: small file in local secure dir. if that's unacceptable for some appliances we document the limitation: no rollback protection. we could also add a hardware-backed monotonic counter option later.
amanda: UX consideration: bundle signing and rotation tooling should produce a rotation_proof chain automatically so operators don't have to manually stitch proofs. CLI will output a single sealed bundle file.
airgap-bot: validation: signed chain OK for bundle sha256:3f5e...; lease_seq 42; prev_bundle_hash matches agent checkpoint.
raj: remaining open: format versioning for rotation_proof and how to handle partial-applies (interrupted upgrades). propose: agent writes a "apply_in_progress" marker before switching content and only marks success after verification. on restart, if marker present, agent attempts rollback to previous content using stored previous_hash or signals operator.
amanda: yep. I'll draft an RFC update with these points: sequence-based lease, signed rotation proof, prev_bundle_hash chain, explicit recovery flow, apply_in_progress marker semantics, and optional HSM integration. tagging you all for review. :sparkles:
liz: thanks — will review for edge cases. :mag:
